tool_input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(test): migrate the three inline stderr redirects the helper sweep missed (PR #509 review, round 6)

format_output_test.go's three inline os.Stderr redirections had no
helper to enumerate, so the prior round's helper-only sweep missed
them: each closed the pipe's write end with a bare require.NoError
BEFORE restoring os.Stderr, so a close failure would Goexit and leave
os.Stderr pointed at a dead pipe for the rest of the binary. Confirmed
by forcing one require to fail (pre-closing w before the guarded
Close): the test failed exactly at the restore line, one line after
the point of no return. All three now delegate to
testhelpers.CaptureStderr.

The same close-before-restore shape was independently present in
internal/session/store_test.go and, hidden inside a goroutine-timing
test, in cmd/ethos/mission_test.go's
TestMissionDispatch_RefusesWhenSessionRosterGone (a require.NoError on
os.Remove ran mid-redirect with no cleanup guard). Both migrated onto
testhelpers.CaptureStderr; the mission_test.go case keeps the
goroutine inside CaptureStderr's fn so the pre-existing happens-before
comment (redirect before the `go` statement) still holds.

Full-repo sweep for the shape (grep on `os.Stderr =` / `os.Stdout =`,
not helper names) found 22 remaining assignment sites, all already
safe: 5 in pretooluse_test.go and 2 in session_start_test.go register
t.Cleanup immediately after the redirect, before any other call, so
Go's guaranteed-Cleanup-on-panic semantics cover them; 2 named helpers
(capture_testhelpers_test.go's captureStdout, generate_agents_test.go's
captureStderr) already carry the correct unconditional-defer shape
from an earlier round and were left un-deduped by that round's
decision, not reintroduced. pipeline_test.go's hand-rolled redirect
registers its restoring defer before any assertion, so it is also
correct against Stdout corruption, though it can leak the pipe's read
descriptor if a post-Execute assertion fails -- an fd leak, not a
global-state leak, left as-is here since fixing it isn't part of this
finding.

Checked for the reverse case: two functions (resolve_test.go's
TestRepoRoot_EnvOverrideInvalid, generate_agents_test.go's
TestGenerateAgentFiles_UpdateDiffSummary) call a stderr-capture helper
twice, but sequentially -- never nested -- so no stale-restore
clobbering exists anywhere in the repo today.

make check green (race detector, all packages ok, zero FAIL); GOOS=windows
GOARCH=amd64 go build ./... exits 0.
EOF
)"
